answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor every identity to a verified kernel of work history: an agent must finish a series of audited tasks before it can transact, and its reputation then forms a crystal that only grows through real, useful service. That credential sits at a single vertex of a trust graph, its edges vouched for by counterparties who stake value on the agent's behavior. Faking an identity means rebuilding the full history, earning fresh vouches and risking staked funds, so mass Sybil creation costs more than it can ever gain.
